target_customer: Home builders and general contractors that use Procore or QuickBooks and receive large volumes of subcontractor invoices
problem: Builders receive thousands of subcontractor invoices per project that must be checked against budgets, approved, paid and entered in accounting by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for invoice processing and payables

founders.name: Ty Sharp
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was CFO of an Aspen general contractor with $350M in construction volume; the launch post also says CFO of a large luxury home builder.

founders.name: Ian Sharp
founders.background_notes: Brother of Ty. The launch post names Gainfully, the founder Q&A names Finvera, as the startup he helped get acquired; sources conflict.

technical_complexity.rationale: Invoice capture, matching to commitments and cost codes, and sync to Procore and QuickBooks is mostly integration work, with some difficulty in extraction accuracy.

defensibility.rationale: Deep Procore and accounting integrations create some lock-in, but generic AP automation vendors can add construction features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy of the wedge was found; a 2021 Built press release shows billing features already existed for builders.

market_need_then: Home builders process heavy invoice volume manually, and the founders came from builder CFO roles; the company reports $450M of invoice volume processed in a 12 month window, self reported.

branding.domain_note: Site at inbuild.ai; earlier domain history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press or community content about the name; the name is a plain compound that describes the building focus.

outcome_analysis: inBuild remains active and sells AI invoice processing to home builders on Procore and QuickBooks, with self reported volumes and customer logos. Its founders came from builder CFO roles, which fits the niche, but no verified funding or independent traction data was found, so the outcome story is incomplete.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators conflict, with one reporting $500K pre-seed in April 2023 and another reporting about $2.75M across two pre-seed rounds with HomeTeam Ventures and Greater Colorado Venture Fund; no company or press confirmation found. The company site lists YC, HomeTeam VC and Howdy.vc as partners without amounts. No competitor coverage dated near the batch was found. Both founder education fields are unknown. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed of 2023-04 is recorded from VCBacked and Bouncewatch; Bouncewatch also lists a 2.25M pre-seed dated 2020-09 that is not recorded because it predates the batch and conflicts with other sources.
